catalog_quote: 3.9. Lengthening of a. All Western communalects (WAY, KBY, NKR, MGD, TBW, BRV, BTW, TBI, and YML) have a rule of a-lengthening, which operates at phrase level: phrase-antepenultimate a is lengthened (and probably also constitutes an intonation peak). These examples are from Tubai: 'nā waqa' 'the boat'; 'na waqāvuka' 'the airplane'; 'na vānua' 'the land'; 'na vanuā kō' 'this land'. 3.10. Diphthongization. In all languages under study except those of Lau (LAU and VBL), the penultimate stress rule is qualified by the rule that stress always falls on the first vowel of a low or mid to high vowel sequence. In Lau, however, there is no qualification to the penultimate stress rule, so it is the second vowel of such a sequence that is stressed when it occurs in penultimate position. Thus we may contrast: NWN 'ráica' 'see it' / LAU 'raíca'; ONO 'ráuta' 'enough' / VBL 'raúta'. ... such sequences …

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel/mora of the word (the 'measure-penultimate stress' Geraghty attributes to Schütz 1976 for Fijian generally), with one qualification: in a rising vowel sequence (low or mid vowel followed by a high vowel, e.g. ai, au), stress goes to the first vowel of the sequence (ráica, ráuta), i.e. such sequences behave as diphthongs. In the Western communalects, which include the three NNS communalects Batiwai, Tubai and Yemalu that make up namo1248, there is in addition a phrase-level rule lengthening the phrase-antepenultimate a (which 'probably also constitutes an intonation peak'): Tubai nā waqa, na waqāvuka, na vānua, na vanuā kō.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed for these communalects; the phrase-antepenultimate a-lengthening is described as probably an intonation peak, not as secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Lau (LAU, VBL) lacks the diphthong qualification (stress on the second vowel of a rising sequence in penultimate position); the Western a-lengthening rule applies only to a and only at phrase level.
new_statements.domain_note: The penultimate rule is a word/measure-level statement made for all 38 communalects surveyed (Geraghty treats stress as Fijian-wide, drawing on Schütz's 'measure' analysis of Standard Fijian); the a-lengthening rule is explicitly phrase-level and illustrated with noun phrases from Tubai (a bwb dialect). No instrumental data.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog namo1248 = dialects Batiwai (bati1252), Nalea (nale1237), Tubai (tuba1276). In Geraghty 1979 these correspond to the Western Fijian 'NNS' group — Batiwai (BTW), Tubai (TBI), Yemalu (YML) — defined on p. 273; the stress statement (p. 68) is made for all 38 communalects surveyed and the a-lengthening rule for the Western communalects including BTW/TBI/YML, with the phrase examples from Tubai. Geraghty's 'Namosi (NMS)' communalect proper (Namosi province villages) is classified by him as Eastern Fijian (South East Viti Levu), not part of NNS, although the Glottolog/hh.bib language code mapping also lists 'Namosi' under bwb.
